elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: § 19.1 (retained verbatim): "Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form."

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: § 19.1: "Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications"; § 1.7 expressly defines Services to include "the hosted software", and amended § 19.2 warrants each Deliverable conforms to its documentation for ninety (90) days.

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: § 19.1's conformance warranty for Services (which includes the hosted software) states no duration at all; it may be read as continuing (better than 12 months) or as speaking only at delivery. No express 12-month period appears in the rendered language, and amended § 19.2 fixes only a 90-day Deliverable period.
§ 19.1's Services warranties are untimed and, as amended, the § 19.2 cut-off is scoped "for that Deliverable", so no 15-day (or any) expiry now truncates the Services warranty below 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: § 19.4 (unchanged): "Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge."
§ 19.4: "Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it" if Vendor cannot cure within a reasonable period.

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: The rationale asserts § 19.3 carries an Applicable Law compliance warranty, but § 19.3 is not among the rendered operative paragraphs, so its text cannot be verified here.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: § 19.3 is not rendered; the drafter reports it is narrowed to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor", which would fall short of an unqualified no-malicious-code warranty, but the operative text is unavailable for inspection.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: § 1.7 defines "Services" to expressly include "the hosted software", and § 19.1 warrants that Services "will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications" with no expiry; the amended § 19.2 cut-off is limited to "that Deliverable", so it cannot truncate the software warranty. Duration therefore equals or exceeds 90 days.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: § 19.1 warranties on Services (workmanlike performance and documentation conformance) run without a stated cut-off, and the only durational limit (§ 19.2, now 90 days) is expressly confined to Deliverables.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: § 19.4: "For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge."
§ 19.4: refund of Fees paid for the affected item where Vendor cannot re-perform, repair or replace within a reasonable period — a customary cure-first refund, retained unchanged.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the rendered language: the 15-day Deliverable conformance period is raised to ninety (90) days, the untimed § 19.1 Services/hosted-software conformance warranty survives, and § 19.4's repair/replace plus refund remedies are retained verbatim.

Preferred level is not reached: there is no express 12-month software conformance period (§ 19.1 states no duration and § 19.2 sets only 90 days), and the compliance-with-laws and no-malicious-code elements sit in an unrendered § 19.3 that cannot be verified here (the drafter itself reports the malicious-code warranty is narrowed to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor").

Minimality holds: the edit touches only § 19.2 — a numeric change from fifteen to ninety days plus the three-word scoping phrase "for that Deliverable". The scoping is not cosmetic: without it the unqualified cut-off, cross-referenced by § 19.4 ("Section 19.1 or 19.2"), is a contradictory retained sentence that could be argued to extinguish correction and refund obligations for the § 19.1 Services/hosted-software warranties that supply fallback elements 1 and 2. No survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra damages category was added.

Intent is preserved: § 19.4's cross-reference to Sections 19.1 and 19.2 remains accurate, the non-exclusive-remedy carve-outs for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims are untouched, and no defined term is left dangling.

If the team wants the preferred position rather than the fallback, the operative repairs are: (a) add an express twelve (12) month conformance warranty for the hosted software (or state that § 19.1's conformance warranty runs for the Subscription Term), and (b) delete "intentionally introduced by Vendor" from § 19.3 so the malicious-code warranty is unqualified. Per the playbook these are rationale notes, not separate deviations.
